Relevant Text: Introduction ZimmermannLaband syndrome (ZLS [MIM: 135500]) is a rare developmental disorder characterized by facial dysmorphism with bulbous nose and thick ﬂoppy ears, gingival enlargement, intellectual disability (ID) with or without epilepsy, hypoplasia or aplasia of terminal phalanges and nails, hypertrichosis, joint hyperextensibility, and hepatosplenomegaly.1–4 In a proportion of subjects with ZLS, de novo missense variants in KCNH1 (MIM: 603305) has been identiﬁed.5 At the same time, heterozygous KCNH1 missense variants have been reported in individuals with TempleBaraitser syndrome (TBS [MIM: 611816]) which shows considerable phenotypic overlap with ZLS.6 With the identiﬁcation of additional KCNH1mutation positive individuals, the great clinical variability became apparent;7–9 however, a core phenotype of severe ID, neonatal hypotonia, hypertelorism, broad nasal tip, wide mouth, nail aplasia or hypoplasia, a proximal implanted and long thumb, and long great toes was deﬁned.9 KCNH1 encodes the Eag1 (Kv10.1) channel which belongs to the ethera`-gogo family of voltagegated channels.
